answer: Each of 141 aliases needs its own dues histories, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. A union membership history with dues receipts works as the gate: dues receipts from one union stretching back years. The ledge check is what stops the copy-paste farm: The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The tide record is public, the forge cost is per identity, and 141 aliases cost 141 times one honest seat.
